pipeline.built: PDS3 reader + MOLA MEGDR fetcher (scripts/fetch_mola.py, needs internet). This offline build runs on the labelled synthetic fixture.
Label/file validation, pixel-exact clip, grid-alignment check; documented cubic resampling to 1/512° routing and 1/1024° analysis grids.
Slope (spherical spacing), 3x3 local relief, MOLA coverage flags.
Science-proximity field, derived rim target, cell inspection.
8-connected graph on the 1/512° routing grid (native 1/128° kept for comparison), spherical step lengths.
Weighted-sum objective, 3 priority modes; exact least-cost search (Dijkstra on 1/512°, A* on 1/128°).
WHY panel: values, cost breakdown, method, provenance, limitation.
Brief generated from computed route + provenance; printable.

properties.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance landing site)
properties.source: NASA named the Mars 2020 landing site on 5 March 2021; published coordinates 18.4447°N, 77.4508°E (≈18°26'N 77°27'E). Cited value — no local source file, not re-checked in the offline build, so it is not marked VERIFIED.
properties.why: Documented, real starting point on the crater floor.
properties.limitation: Position precision ~0.01°; one MOLA cell is ~0.008°.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Jezero crater (centre)
properties.source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature value (18.38°N, 77.58°E). Cited value — no local source file, not re-checked in the offline build, so it is not marked VERIFIED.
properties.why: Reference point used to locate the crater rim.
properties.limitation: Nomenclature centre, not a surveyed point.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Western delta front
properties.source: NASA describes the fan-shaped sedimentary deposit (delta) west of the landing site; position here is an approximate placement from published maps.
properties.why: Deltas form where a river entered a lake; their layered sediments can record past water and environments.
properties.investigate: Layering, grain size and composition of sedimentary rocks exposed at the front.
properties.limitation: APPROXIMATE position — verify against the real MOLA hillshade / HiRISE before presenting. Composition is not measured by MOLA.
properties.offline_review: Not refined in the offline v2 build (2026-10-10): the only local terrain is the SYNTHETIC fixture, which carries no evidence about the real delta. The fan-shaped bump in the fixture is generated by scripts/make_fixture.py and must not be used to move this point. Check it in QGIS with real CTX/MOLA data (docs/DATA.md).
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

properties.name: Jezero west rim crest (derived)
properties.source: Highest synthetic-fixture elevation (-2196 m) sampled along the azimuth from the crater centre through the landing site, between 0.70 and 1.35 crater radii (found at 1.00 R).
properties.why: Impact-crater rims expose material uplifted from depth; a rim position also gives the crew a regional overview.
properties.investigate: Rim-forming rock types and their relation to crater-floor and delta deposits.
properties.limitation: Located on SYNTHETIC terrain: this point is a pipeline demonstration, not the real rim crest. Located from ~463 m topography only; the exact crest and access path need HiRISE-scale data.
properties.fixture_note: Shown on SYNTHETIC terrain — terrain values near this point are not real.

discover.label: SCIENCE STOP 02
discover.why: Impact-crater rims expose material uplifted from depth; a rim position also gives the crew a regional overview.
discover.investigate: Rim-forming rock types and their relation to crater-floor and delta deposits.
discover.source: Highest synthetic-fixture elevation (-2196 m) sampled along the azimuth from the crater centre through the landing site, between 0.70 and 1.35 crater radii (found at 1.00 R).
discover.limitation: Located on SYNTHETIC terrain: this point is a pipeline demonstration, not the real rim crest. Located from ~463 m topography only; the exact crest and access path need HiRISE-scale data.

method: Dijkstra (scipy.sparse.csgraph, compiled) on the 1/512° routing grid (cubic-spline interpolation (scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates, order=3, prefilter=True; edges padded 8 cells by odd reflection) of the native 1/128° grid; shot counts by nearest neighbour) — 8-connected, spherical step lengths, optimal and deterministic.
Slope evidence also read along the path on the 1/1024° analysis grid (max 12.35°). Finer grids are interpolated and add no terrain detail.
Cell cost c = β + α·T + γ·(1−S) with α=6.0, β=1.0, γ=0.0 (TRAVERSABILITY-FIRST).
Candidate science stop = target within 1200 m of the route.
uncertainty: Terrain source resolution ~463 m per cell (1/128°); the finer route grid is interpolated, so metre-scale obstacles (boulders, small craters) are still not represented.
No orbital imagery (CTX, HiRISE) or composition data (CRISM) integrated; the SURFACE layer is shaded relief computed from the same elevation grid.
Cost-model weights are configurable assumptions, not human mobility limits.
Candidate science targets come from published descriptions or derived topography — not new detections.
Target positions marked APPROXIMATE are placements, not surveyed points.

evidence.name: SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE in MOLA MEGDR binary format — NOT NASA DATA
evidence.detail: none (synthetic) · none — file layout mimics MOLA MEGDR · megt_fixture — synthetic topography

evidence.name: Shaded relief (computed from elevation — not imagery)
evidence.detail: hillshade = cos(angle between surface normal and a sun at azimuth 315°, altitude 45°), 3x vertical exaggeration, on the 1/1024° analysis grid

evidence.name: Slope (1/512° routing grid)
evidence.detail: slope = atan(sqrt((dz/dx)^2 + (dz/dy)^2)), central differences, dx = dy*cos(lat), on the 1/512° routing grid

evidence.name: Science proximity S
evidence.detail: S = max_k exp(-d_k^2 / (2*1500 m^2)) over candidate science targets

method: Dijkstra (scipy.sparse.csgraph, compiled) on the 1/512° routing grid (cubic-spline interpolation (scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates, order=3, prefilter=True; edges padded 8 cells by odd reflection) of the native 1/128° grid; shot counts by nearest neighbour) — 8-connected, spherical step lengths, optimal and deterministic.
Slope evidence also read along the path on the 1/1024° analysis grid (max 18.33°). Finer grids are interpolated and add no terrain detail.
Cell cost c = β + α·T + γ·(1−S) with α=1.5, β=1.0, γ=4.0 (SCIENCE-FIRST).
Candidate science stop = target within 1200 m of the route.
uncertainty: Terrain source resolution ~463 m per cell (1/128°); the finer route grid is interpolated, so metre-scale obstacles (boulders, small craters) are still not represented.
No orbital imagery (CTX, HiRISE) or composition data (CRISM) integrated; the SURFACE layer is shaded relief computed from the same elevation grid.
Cost-model weights are configurable assumptions, not human mobility limits.
Candidate science targets come from published descriptions or derived topography — not new detections.
Target positions marked APPROXIMATE are placements, not surveyed points.
SYNTHETIC TEST TERRAIN: every terrain number in this brief is from the synthetic fixture, not NASA data.
